To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

affine transformations of the spatial covariance matrices can significantly improve classification performances when data from different sessions are considered, as well as when data from different subjects are considered.
we propose an affine transformation to align the covariance matrices of the different sessions/subjects and we use it to improve the classification performances of the BCI system.
the proposed affine transformation provides a significant improvement in terms of classification performance, when applied to the problem of EEG-based BCI transfer learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of cross-session and/or cross-subject classification in BCI applications.
the problem of cross-subject and cross-session transfer learning for EEG-based BCI classification.
the problem of transfer classification in BCI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the affine transformation proposed is able to significantly improve the performances in cross-session and cross-user BCI classification.
transfer learning is possible in the BCI context, and that the affine transformation is a powerful tool to achieve such a transfer.
our method is a powerful approach to tackle the problem of transfer-learning in the context of EEG-based brain-computer interfaces, providing an improvement in the classification performances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the affine transformation is an effective method for transfer learning in the Riemann manifold framework.
we have developed an efficient and effective transfer learning framework based on the R-SPD geometry.
we provide a framework for transfer learning in the Riemann manifold of positive symmetric matrices, which has been shown to be very effective for the BCI application.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the affine transformation proposed allows for a better initialization of the classifier and for a better estimation of the covariance matrices, leading to a more reliable and robust classification performance.

transfer learning can be achieved by simply aligning data from different sessions or subjects, and then applying a standard classification method, without resorting to sophisticated machine learning techniques.

the affine transformation can be used in any application that involves the analysis of data represented as SPD matrices, such as EEG-based BCIs, but also fMRI-based BCIs, and other neuroimaging applications, such as the analysis of resting-state functional connectivity.
